# Index

8 cases, newest first. Each line: title — kind, from to to; how far the claims can be checked; the author's stake in the tools; the cost the source gives; a one-line summary.

Lessons drawn from the cases, by aspect: [lessons/index.md](lessons/index.md) (119 lessons on 16 pages). Before a migration: [checklist.md](checklist.md).

- [GitHub moves its Copilot agent runtime from TypeScript to Rust using agents](cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md) — language, TypeScript on Node.js and V8 to Rust (native library with a C ABI); evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$120,000 for ~136.3 billion tokens (engineer time not priced). One engineer steered agent fleets to port about 430,000 lines of TypeScript to Rust in place, one component per PR, over 14.5 weeks.
- [Intel's IDEAS harness ports the libgit2 command-line client from C to safe Rust](cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md) — language, C (libgit2 command-line client) to safe Rust (no unsafe code); evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$0.55 per symbol for translation (total unstated), plus ~$6.5 for repair. An LLM harness turned 112K lines of C into safe Rust that compiled but crashed; 8 person-hours guiding an agent got git blame working.
- [Bun moves its JavaScript runtime off Zig onto Rust with Claude agents in 11 days](cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md) — language, Zig (Bun runtime, bundler, package manager, test runner) to Rust (about 100 crates); evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$165,000 at API list prices for the tokens used before merge (690 million output tokens, 5.9 billion fresh input tokens, 72 billion cached input tokens). One engineer ran about 50 Claude Code workflows, up to 64 agents at once, to port 535K lines of Zig to Rust; all tests passed and it merged in 11 days.
- [1Password uses AI agents to refactor its Go monolith and begin a service extraction](cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md) — architecture, Go monolith (B5), database transactions opened with MustBegin (panics on failure) to separately owned services; transaction calls that return errors; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents rewrote over 3,000 panicking transaction calls from a tight spec, but stumbled on a service extraction's ordering and invariants.
- [Spotify runs fleet-wide migrations with its Honk background coding agent](cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md) — mixed, many (for example Java AutoValue classes, old Scio versions, deprecated datasets) to many (for example Java records, the newest Scio, new dataset versions); evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. Spotify put a coding agent inside its fleet migration tooling; verifiers and an LLM judge gate each PR, and over 1,500 agent PRs were merged.
- [Google widens int32 IDs to int64 in 39 migrations with an LLM pipeline](cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md) — data, int32 ID fields in protocol buffer schemas and the code using them (Java, C++, Dart and others) to int64 ID fields; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. A nightly pipeline of code search, rule-based sorting, an internal Gemini model and staged checks drafted 74.45% of 595 code changes in 39 ID migrations.
- [Airbnb moves 3.5K React test files off Enzyme onto React Testing Library](cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (React component tests) to React Testing Library; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. An LLM pipeline with per-file validation steps and retries migrated 97% of about 3,500 React test files; people finished the rest by hand.
- [Slack pairs a syntax-tree codemod with Claude 2.1 to help move 15K Enzyme tests to React Testing Library](cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (React unit and integration tests) to React Testing Library; evidence: shown-in-source; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Codemod alone 45% (evaluation files), Claude 2.1 alone 40-60% (base not given), both 80% of code in 9 checked files; 22% of tests passed over 338 files.
